Hi Alyssa — thanks for the forecast and the timelines.

We can absolutely put a short, procurement-ready proposal together. Early thoughts based on your ask:
- 12-month price hold at your current per-token rate if HelioPay signs a 12-month committed tier at +20% of current committed tokens.
- One-time operational credit: two options we can take to procurement — $45k credit (standard bridge) or $60k credit with a 12-month commit + 30% overage protection for Q4 peak.
- Amendment will include a rollback clause: if committed usage drops below 85% of the floor for two consecutive months, we re-open pricing review.

I’ve attached a proposed amendment and a pricing workbook with both scenarios. Can you confirm whether procurement prefers a single line-item credit or an amortized credit across invoices? That will change the amendment wording slightly.

I’ll loop in Lauren to confirm approval path for the higher credit if needed. Monica will help scope the exact commit tiers in the workbook.

Best,

Ben/Team — reviewed. Finance is comfortable approving the $60k one-time credit under these conditions:
- HelioPay signs the 12-month amendment with a +20% committed floor (commit baseline defined as the average of the last three invoice months).
- Price hold is defined as the explicit per-token invoice line effective on the prior term end date.
- 30% overage protection applies only for the first 90 days after amendment effective date and covers billable overage up to the 30% cap; overage beyond that is billed at the hold rate.
- If committed usage falls below 85% of the committed floor for two consecutive months after month 6, finance can trigger a review (rollback clause).

I’ve reviewed the pricing workbook — net ARR impact is acceptable given the retention probability and expansion signals. Lauren, if you’re good to present this to the customer, we can finalize the redline and send to Alyssa (I’ll authorize the credit).

Alyssa — thanks for your patience.

Summary of agreed commercial terms (ready for procurement/legal):
- Term: 12 months from amendment effective date.
- Commit: +20% of current committed tokens (baseline = average of last 3 invoice months).
- Price hold: Redwood will hold the per-token invoice line rate in effect at term start for 12 months.
- One-time operational credit: $60,000 applied as a single line-item on the first invoice after the amendment effective date.
- Overage protection: 30% coverage for the first 90 days after amendment effective date for billable usage above the committed floor.
- Rollback: If committed usage drops below 85% of the floor for two consecutive months after month 6, Redwood may re-open pricing review.

I’ve attached the redlined amendment and the final pricing workbook. If that matches your procurement/legal needs I’ll route the DocuSign package for signature this afternoon.
